conclusion.label: endorses

report:
The claim is **not false**—the evidence strongly supports that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, brand name Shingrix) reduces shingles in adults aged 70 years or older.

**Key evidence:**

1. **ZOE-70 pivotal trial (NEJM 2016):** In this randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 13,900 adults aged ≥70 (mean age 75.6), the HZ/su vaccine significantly reduced the risk of herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia. The authors concluded the vaccine "reduced the risk of herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia among adults 70 years of age or older, without substantial safety concerns" (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800).

2. **ZOE-50 trial (NEJM 2015):** This companion trial in adults ≥50 showed vaccine efficacy was high, and efficacy in adults ≥70 was similar to that in younger participants (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184).

3. **Real-world effectiveness:** A 2025 study in *Annals of Internal Medicine* using Medicare claims data confirmed real-world effectiveness of RZV in older adults (https://www.med.unc.edu/fammed/2025/10/21/unc-study-confirms-shingles-vaccine-effectiveness-in-older-adults/). A 2025 *Clinical Infectious Diseases* study also evaluated real-world vaccine effectiveness in adults ≥50 (https://academic.oup.com/cid/article/81/6/e717/8171839).

4. **Long-term protection:** Extension studies of ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 show durable protection lasting at least 10 years (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8904019/).

5. **CDC recommendation:** CDC recommends two doses of RZV for all adults ≥50, with no upper age limit (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html).

**Conclusion:** The claim is well-supported by multiple randomized trials, real-world studies, and long-term follow-up data. The vaccine demonstrably reduces shingles incidence in adults aged 70 and older.
